identity.mechanic: you groom one magnificent, ridiculous knight who holds the lek alone at dawn. The rest of the order are squires and elders who feed him, and hens who sit in the bilberry and judge. Each year the order gets smaller and its last knights get grander. The tribe offers few units, each one enormous, on a board full of deliberate gaps.

keywords.name: Duel
keywords.text: *Start of Combat: this and the enemy across hit each other once with their Attack.* If the slot across is empty, it Duels a random enemy in that row instead; if that row is empty, nothing happens. A unit in your back row therefore Duels the enemy back row. A unit **wins** a Duel if the enemy dies and it survives. A Duel is a rite, not an attack, so the rules that say "when attacked" or "attacking" (Hunker, Nightshade, Bitter, Mire, Cleave, Pack) don't apply. Shield, Bristle and Damage Reduction still do. "Duels X" on a card means the same exchange against X. If both units have Shield, both Shields pop and neither wins. Duels follow Start of Combat order, so between two Duel boards the side that attacks first Duels first.

keywords.name: Proud
keywords.text: A unit is Proud while no friendly unit is **beside** it (left or right in its row). Diagonal neighbours don't count. Any unit beside it breaks Proud, Created ones too (a Bird's Egg, a summon). It's checked when an effect asks, so a unit summoned beside it mid-fight breaks it from then on. Since gaps never close, you build Proud boards by leaving slots empty. A full Proud board has at most 4 units (for example F1, F3, B1, B3).

keywords.name: Champion
keywords.text: Your **biggest Knight**; on a tie, the first in reading order. It's re-checked whenever an effect asks, so it can change mid-fight when the Champion dies. **Hens** (Bilberry Hen, Dame Reisig) belong to the tribe but are not Knights, so they are never Champion.

identity.plays: Early on, Duel bodies win fights by killing the enemy across before the fight begins. From Tier 2 you choose what to feed. One path feeds the *Champion*: squires are sold or crossed out into him, and empty slots pay him. Another feeds *Proud* units: a chequerboard of four isolated knights, each paid for standing alone. The third feeds *Duel wins*: hens and the Cork-Pop Master turn every win into growth. All three overlap. A Proud Champion who wins Duels is fed by every card in the tribe, so the puzzle is how few units you can field and still survive. Start of Combat resolves in reading order, so where you put a unit decides whether the Shield lands before or after the Duel. Keeping slots empty costs you: the side with more units attacks first, and survivors deal hero damage. The Knights pay that price on purpose.

units.name: Squire Konrad
units.text: End of Turn: if he is Proud, he permanently gains +1/+1. When sold: your Champion permanently gains his stats.
units.golden: End of Turn: if Proud, permanently gain +2/+2. When sold: your Champion permanently gains his stats.

units.name: Pennon-Squire
units.text: When played: give another unit Duel and +1/+1, permanently.
units.golden: When played: give another unit Duel and +2/+2, permanently.

units.name: Bilberry Hen *(Hen)*
units.text: Whenever a friendly unit wins a Duel, it permanently gains +1/+1, or +2/+2 if it's Proud.
units.golden: Whenever a friendly unit wins a Duel, it permanently gains +2/+2, or +4/+4 if it's Proud.

units.name: Refectory Prior
units.text: Start of Turn: if your tier is 3 or higher and you have 4 or fewer units, gain 1 gold. With 3 or fewer, gain 2 instead.
units.golden: Start of Turn: if your tier is 3 or higher and you have 4 or fewer units, gain 2 gold. With 3 or fewer, gain 4 instead.

units.name: Sir Hartmut the Whetting
units.text: Duel. When he wins a Duel, he Duels a random front-row enemy (back row once the front row is empty). Twice a fight.
units.golden: Duel. When he wins a Duel, he Duels a random front-row enemy (back row once the front row is empty). Four times a fight.

units.name: Fantail Warden
units.text: Start of Combat: if this is Proud, give your Champion Shield.
units.golden: Start of Combat: if Proud, give your two biggest Knights Shield.

units.name: Elder of the Centre
units.text: End of Turn: your Champion permanently gains +1/+1 for each empty slot on your board.

units.name: Grit-Pit Forager
units.text: End of Turn: if this is Proud, get a Gizzard Stone.
units.golden: End of Turn: if Proud, get 2 Gizzard Stones.

units.name: Sir Brennbart the Mad
units.text: Duel. He Duels the enemy's biggest unit, in either row, instead of the one across.
units.golden: Duel. He Duels the enemy's biggest unit, then its second biggest.

units.name: Scarlet-Brow Marshal
units.text: End of Turn: your Proud units permanently gain +2/+2.

units.name: Master of the Cork-Pop
units.text: Effects that trigger when a unit wins a Duel trigger twice, and their limits double too ("Twice a fight" becomes four times).
units.golden: Effects that trigger when a unit wins a Duel trigger three times, and their limits triple too.

units.name: Sprucehold Envoy
units.text: When played: Discover a Knight. If you have 4 or fewer other units, Discover a second.
units.golden: When played: Discover a Knight from one tier higher. If you have 4 or fewer other units, Discover a second.

units.name: The Chronicler
units.text: Start of Turn: if you have 4 or more units, you may destroy your smallest unit other than this and your Champion. If you do, your Champion permanently gains twice its stats.
units.golden: Start of Turn: if you have 4 or more units, you may destroy your smallest unit other than this and your Champion. If you do, your Champion permanently gains four times its stats.

units.name: Dame Reisig, the Grey Hen *(Hen)*
units.text: Your Champion is your biggest unit of any tribe, not just Knights. End of Turn: your Champion permanently gains +3/+3 for each Proud unit you have.

units.name: Herald of the Last Dawn
units.text: Start of Combat: your Champion Duels a random front-row enemy (back row once the front row is empty) once for each empty slot on your board, at most 3 times.
units.golden: Start of Combat: your Champion Duels a random front-row enemy (back row once the front row is empty) once for each empty slot on your board, at most 6 times.

units.name: Grand Master Ottokar
units.text: Your Proud units have Duel. Each of your units takes no damage in its first Duel each fight.
units.golden: Your Proud units have Duel. Each of your units takes no damage in its first two Duels each fight.

units.name: Sir Gottfried, Last of Sprucehold
units.text: Start of Combat: for this fight, he gains +50% of his current stats for each empty slot on your board, all counted from those stats (6 empty slots: x4).
units.golden: Start of Combat: for this fight, he gains +100% of his current stats for each empty slot on your board, all counted from those stats (6 empty slots: x7).

units.name: Sir Altmark of the Trophy Wall
units.text: Whenever your Champion wins a Duel, it permanently gains a quarter of the loser's stats as they were before the Duel.
units.golden: Whenever your Champion wins a Duel, it permanently gains half of the loser's stats as they were before the Duel.

extras.name: Gizzard Stone
extras.text: Item. Give a unit +2/+2 permanently. If it's your Champion, +4/+4 instead.

builds.name: A. The Last Knight (lone Champion).
builds.text: Use Squire Konrad, Elder of the Centre, The Chronicler, Herald of the Last Dawn and Sir Gottfried. You grow one Knight by selling and crossing out the units around him, and the empty slots pay him every turn. By the end you field two or three units: Gottfried as Champion, Herald and perhaps a Fantail Warden for his Shield. Herald Duels before the fight starts. Gottfried then multiplies himself by the empty board. The Chronicler wants 4 units at Start of Turn, but the Elder and Gottfried want few at End of Turn and in the fight. So each turn you buy a fat unit for the Chronicler to cross out, and you fight small. Konrad, grown Proud in a corner, is the best thing to feed him: a 6/7 Konrad crossed out gives +26.

builds.name: B. The Proud Court (chequerboard).
builds.text: Use Scarlet-Brow Marshal, Grit-Pit Forager, Fantail Warden, Dame Reisig and Ottokar. Four units sit at F1, F3, B1 and B3 or similar, with no one beside anyone. Marshal and Reisig grow all four, and Forager turns its isolation into Gizzard Stones. Ottokar gives the whole court Duel and makes each first Duel free, so four enemies take a hit before the fight. The Proud board is also immune to Cleave by construction.

builds.name: C. Dawn Duellists (wide Duel chains).
builds.text: Use Fir-Ridge Yearling, Pennon-Squire, Bilberry Hen, Sir Hartmut, Master of the Cork-Pop and Sir Altmark. Here the Knights are allowed a full board, and every unit Duels. Each win feeds the Hen. The Cork-Pop doubles the Hen, Hartmut's re-Duels and Altmark's trophies. Sir Brennbart Duels the enemy carry in the back row to soften it before the fight. Pennon-Squire gives Duel to anything, so this build takes other tribes in.

builds.name: Mixing with other tribes in a lobby
builds.text:
- **Oozes:** units inside a **Belly** aren't on the board, so an Ooze can hold your court while the empty slots pay Elder, Herald and Gottfried. If The Chronicler crosses out a full Ooze at Start of Turn, the units in its Belly come back out onto your board. With Dame Reisig, a huge Ooze can be Champion and take every Knight buff, and Eating a grown Konrad keeps his stats.
- **Hunters:** give a Hunter Duel with Pennon-Squire. Its Quarry is also the enemy across, so a Duel kill fires **Take** at Start of Combat.
- **Birds:** Fly South empties a slot for two turns, which feeds the empty-slot cards. The Egg in the Nest is a unit, though, and it breaks Proud beside it. With Reisig, a Bird coming home with doubled stats can become Champion.
- **Bog folk:** Mire and Bitter don't touch Duels, so Knights can clear a Mire wall before it starts taxing attacks.
- **Hedgerow folk:** Pass X goes to your rightmost other unit, so put the Champion at F4 or B3.
- **Neutral Shield units** turn any Duel into a free kill.

risks: **Pre-fight wipes.** Herald, Hartmut, Brennbart, Ottokar and Cork-Pop together could kill most of an enemy front row before anyone attacks, which makes the fight a non-event. Each one is capped, and every Duel costs health (except under Ottokar), but this combination needs a sim first.

**Too few units.** A one- or two-unit board attacks second, deals almost no hero damage when it wins, and loses to many small attackers or summons. That is the intended price, but the Last Knight build could be unplayable or binary. Watch how often it wins against wide boards.

**Gottfried's ceiling.** Alone, he fights at ×4 (×7 golden) of an already-fed Champion. That's well past the Tier 6 in-fight guide, on purpose. If it runs away, change the rate to +50% per empty slot beyond the second.
**The Chronicler is now optional** ("you may"), so it no longer forces a loss; watch whether players skip it so often that the buy-to-cross-out rhythm fades.
**Reading-order puzzles** (Warden's Shield before or after the Champion's Duel) are Johnny's joy and a newcomer's confusion. The UI needs to show Start of Combat order.

**Reisig makes the Knights a support package** for other tribes' carries. That's good for Johnny but could make the Knights a splash rather than a tribe. Watch the pick rate of Reisig without other Knights.
**Refectory Prior now waits for Tier 3** and pays 2 gold at 3 or fewer units. Watch whether 2 a turn makes a three-unit board too rich.

**Rules settled in v2:** Created units beside a unit break Proud; two Shields in a Duel both pop and neither wins; Duels follow Start of Combat order. Which side's Start of Combat goes first is still a Bramble-wide rule to settle.

tier_check.note: Yearling 2/2 Duel is the tempo body at exactly 4. Konrad, the seed, is 1/2 (below body; the value is in his text) and grows +2 a turn when Proud (~0.5 body against ~0.4). His sale banks the stored growth.

all 5–6 body. Pennon-Squire's once value is low in stats (+2) but it hands out a keyword. Bilberry Hen gives 2–6 a turn at 1–3 wins (0.3–1 body), up to twice that on Proud winners. Prior gives 1–2 gold a turn from Tier 3, standard Tier 2 economy that pays only the Knights' small board.

all 7 body. Elder gives 6–10 a turn on a 3–4 unit board (0.8–1.4 body), above the guide when the board is tiny, on purpose. Forager gives 4–8 through stones. Hartmut's up-to-three Duels sit inside the 0.7–1.4 in-fight range at Tier 3 sizes.

8–9 body. Marshal gives 8–16 a turn on 2–4 Proud units (target ~11). Cork-Pop is the first multiplier. Brennbart is an enabler: he reaches the back row. Envoy's one or two Discovers are ~2 bodies of value once.

12 body. Reisig gives 24 at four Proud units (target ~24). Chronicler gives twice the smallest unit, ~20–40 late, at the cost of a unit. Herald's up to three Champion Duels are in-fight value near ~4 bodies.

14–15 body. Altmark scales with the enemy's size, not your own, at ~12–60 a turn (target ~56). Ottokar's free Duels across a court are around the ~6-body in-fight target when the Attack is high, and above it when Duels kill. **Broken on purpose:** Gottfried's in-fight multiplier goes past the guide, because it only works on a board that has given up most of its HP.

rationale: **The fantasy came first:** one vain giant holding the lek while the order shrinks and the hens judge. Everything else had to serve "few, enormous, alone."
**I kept four themes:** display, the dawn duel, being judged and splendid decline. I dropped forest-guarding, snowshoes and the Fence Line because they don't map onto a board.
**Display became Proud,** a rule about gaps. Gaps never close in Bramble, so standing alone is a real, visible board shape, and it caps a Proud board at four.
**The single champion became one named target (Champion),** so that every feeder has an aim and players can steer who holds the title.
**The dawn duel became Duel at Start of Combat.** It is "a rite, not an attack," which is both the flavour and the source of cross-tribe rules interplay with Mire, Hunker and Quarry.
**A back-row Duel hits the back row,** because the lek has stations, and placement should change who you face.
**Decline became empty slots as fuel,** plus selling or crossing out units into the Champion (Konrad, Elder, Chronicler, Gottfried). Shrinking is the engine, not a side effect.
**The judging hens became back-row Hens that reward wins and are never Champion,** as in the seed: "not members, not impressed."
**Dame Reisig is the one bridge that crowns any tribe,** giving Johnny a sanctioned way to use the Knights outside their purpose.
**The multiplier repeats Duel-win triggers, not buffs.** Wins are bounded by the number of enemies and by health lost, which keeps the runaway check simple.
**Each Tier 6 caps one build:** Gottfried the lone Champion, Ottokar the Proud court, Altmark the duellists. Each still pays into the other two.
**Numbers were costed last** against Part C. The places above the guide all depend on a small board, which is the tribe's own cost.

**Shape changes:** Tier 2 has two enablers and one economy piece, as the guide suggests. Tier 4 has no second buffer; Envoy holds the economy slot so that the Knights' small boards still find their pieces.

changes.what: Proud now says Created units beside it break it. Duel settles Shield against Shield and Duel order.
changes.why: The design listed these rules holes, and half the tribe checks Proud every turn.

changes.what: Bilberry Hen gives +2/+2 instead of +1/+1 when the Duel winner is Proud.
changes.why: Hens now judge Proud knights too, so the Duel and Proud builds braid.

changes.what: Refectory Prior pays only from tier 3: 1 gold at 4 or fewer units, 2 at 3 or fewer.
changes.why: Every board had 4 or fewer units early, so it was always the right buy.

changes.what: Sir Hartmut's extra Duels go to the back row once the front row is empty.
changes.why: The card didn't say what happens when the front row is dead.

changes.what: Cork-Pop now doubles the limits too: Hartmut's 'Twice a fight' becomes four times.
changes.why: It was unclear whether extra triggers spent the cap; spending it would make the combo do nothing.

changes.what: The Chronicler's destroy is now 'you may'; the Champion gains only if you do.
changes.why: Keeps the buy-to-cross-out rhythm without a forced loss of a unit you wanted.

changes.what: Herald's Duels go to the back row once the front row is empty.
changes.why: The card didn't say what happens when the front row is dead.

changes.what: Sir Gottfried's gain is counted from his current stats, not compounding, with x4 at six gaps shown.
changes.why: '+50% for each empty slot' could read as compounding.

changes.what: Sir Altmark takes the loser's stats as they were before the Duel.
changes.why: It was unclear whether it used the stats before or after the Duel's damage.
